programs.name: MN Grain Storage Facility Safety Grant
programs.statusNote: Open for FY2026–2027 · first come, first served
programs.pays: 75% of safety equipment, up to $400 per bin and $2,400 per farm each year
programs.warn: Get the signed grant contract BEFORE you buy anything or start work. You’re paid back after the work is done and paid for.
key: For Minnesota farms with on-farm grain bins or silos. One application per farm each state fiscal year.

Covers: burying power lines that run over augers, sweep auger guards or controls, lockout/tagout, shields on moving parts, dust collection, bin level indicators, fall protection (harness, anchors, ladder systems), guardrails/platforms on bins built before June 2020, respirators and hearing protection.
Pays 75% of eligible cost, up to $400 per bin or silo and $2,400 per farm per year.
Applications in by May 1 get priority; later ones may wait until the fiscal year starts July 1. Money runs out first come, first served.
Apply online in the MDA grant system (create an account, pick “FY 2026-2027 Grain Storage Facility Safety Grant”).

steps.t: Make a list of the safety items you want (power line, auger guards, etc.)
steps.help: Use “Your project” below — the app fills in your bins.

steps.t: Get written quotes (and from your electric co-op for burying the line)
Create an account and apply online
Wait for the signed grant contract — don’t buy before this
Call 811 (Gopher State One Call) before anyone digs
Do the work and pay the bills
Send receipts / proof of payment to MDA to get reimbursed

programs.name: EQIP On-Farm Energy
programs.statusNote: Apply any time · Minnesota’s sign-up deadline for 2027 funding was Sept 11, 2026, so a new application will likely wait for the next round
programs.pays: Part of the cost of energy-saving upgrades like a more efficient grain dryer — after an energy audit
programs.warn: Don’t buy or start work until your EQIP contract is signed — costs before that aren’t paid.
key: Minnesota’s sign-up deadline for 2027 EQIP funding was Friday, September 11, 2026. NRCS takes applications any time, but ones after that date usually wait for the next ranking round. Ask your office for the next date.
NRCS cost-share: it pays part of the cost of the practice, after it’s installed and checked.
For a dryer, NRCS usually wants an on-farm energy audit / energy management plan first.
Your farm records must be up to date at FSA (farm & tract numbers, AD-1026 conservation form, income form).
Beginning, veteran and limited-resource farmers can get higher payment rates.
Rates and cutoffs change by state and year — your county USDA Service Center has the final word.

steps.t: Farm records up to date at FSA (farm/tract #, AD-1026, CCC-941, CCC-902)
Call your county USDA Service Center (NRCS) — ask about EQIP On-Farm Energy and sign the application
steps.help: Ask Farm AI: “What do I say when I call?”

steps.t: Energy audit of the dryer and grain system
steps.help: The app has your dryer, bins and propane info for the auditor.

steps.t: Get 2–3 dealer quotes for the same size and features
Application ranked at the cutoff date
Approved → sign the EQIP contract
Install to NRCS standards
Certify it’s done → get paid

programs.name: FSA Farm Storage Facility Loan
programs.statusNote: Apply any time · must be approved before any work
programs.pays: Low-interest loan up to $500,000 for bins, dryers and handling equipment · 15% down (microloan: up to $50,000, 5% down)
programs.warn: The loan must be approved BEFORE any site prep, construction or equipment delivery — even accepting delivery early can make you ineligible.
key: A loan, not a grant — low fixed interest, terms up to 12 years depending on the amount.

Covers storage bins and structures, grain drying equipment, and handling equipment like conveyors, hoppers and dumpers. Ask your office about a bucket leg — it isn’t listed by name. A leg is handling equipment, so it likely won’t fit REAP, EQIP or the MN safety grant. This loan is the best fit for it.
Standard loan: up to $500,000, minimum 15% down. Microloan: up to $50,000, 5% down, less paperwork.
Standard loans need storage needs based on 3 years of production history; microloans can self-certify.
$100 non-refundable application fee. Every loan needs an environmental review before approval.
Apply at the FSA county office that keeps your farm records.

steps.t: Decide what you need (pit, conveyors, bins, dryer) and get quotes
Pull 3 years of production history
steps.help: The app has your bins and harvest records.

steps.t: Apply at your FSA county office (application CCC-185, $100 fee)
Environmental review + loan approval — don’t start before this
Build / install, keep invoices
Loan funds paid out — ask FSA about partial payments during the build

links.t: Farm Storage Facility Loan fact sheet (PDF)

programs.name: Electric co-op efficiency rebates
programs.statusNote: Varies by co-op · call to check
programs.pays: Rebates for LED shop lights, fan speed controls (VFDs), efficient motors, sometimes grain dryers
programs.warn: Many rebates need pre-approval or a spec sheet — ask before you buy.
key: Most electric co-ops offer agricultural and commercial efficiency rebates — the co-op on your bill decides what and how much.
Common: LED lighting for shops and yard lights, variable-speed drives on aeration fans, premium-efficiency motors, sometimes grain dryers.
Ask the co-op about moving or burying lines near bins and augers — they usually have to do or approve that work.
Rebates can often be combined with grants — ask.

steps.t: Call your electric co-op (number on your bill) — ask for ag/commercial efficiency rebates
steps.help: Ask Farm AI for a call script.

steps.t: Ask what needs pre-approval and what paperwork they want
Buy qualifying items (keep spec sheets and invoices)
Send the rebate form + invoices

docs: Product spec sheets (DLC listing for LEDs)

programs.name: USDA REAP (Rural Energy for America)
programs.statusNote: New rules in effect Oct 16, 2026 · not taking applications yet (waiting for USDA’s funding notice)
programs.pays: Part of the cost of energy-efficiency upgrades for your own operation, paid only after the project is built and has a year of real savings data. Not guaranteed.

changed.t: USDA’s new REAP rule took effect Oct 16, 2026. Projects must now be finished and running before you apply (12–24 months after completion), with a year of real savings data. Applications aren’t open yet.

key: New REAP rule took effect October 16, 2026 (USDA is taking comments until November 2, 2026).
Build first, apply later: the project must be completed 12 to 24 months before you apply. For the first application window under the new rule, it can be up to 36 months.
You apply with real numbers: 12 months of energy use after the upgrade plus 12 months from before it.
One application per owner per federal fiscal year, judged in one national competition. USDA will publish yearly application windows in a funding notice, which isn’t out yet.

Energy-efficiency upgrades for your own operation are still covered. The rule uses grain drying as an example, but it doesn’t name grain dryers as eligible. Confirm with your USDA Rural Development office.
If you applied under the old rules and don’t have a signed agreement, you’ll need to apply again under the new rules.
Can a dryer use both EQIP and REAP? Not answered here. Ask NRCS and Rural Development before you buy, because EQIP needs a signed contract first.

steps.t: Pick your dryer path first: EQIP needs a signed contract before you buy; REAP is applied for after it’s installed. Ask NRCS and Rural Development
Before replacing the old dryer, save 12 months of fuel and power bills plus bushels dried (REAP needs a year of “before” numbers)
Install the dryer and keep every invoice
Keep 12 months of fuel, power and bushels-dried records after it’s running
Watch for USDA’s REAP funding notice (the app checks weekly)
Apply in a window that opens 12–24 months after the project was finished (up to 36 months for the first window)

docs: 12 months of energy bills before the upgrade
12 months of energy bills after it’s running

old.pays: Has paid grants for energy-efficiency upgrades like grain dryers in past years
key: In April 2026 USDA rescinded the FY2025–2027 REAP funding notice. New applications will open after the updated regulation is published.
If you applied before and don’t have a signed agreement, you’ll need to apply again under the new rules.
Good to prepare now: an energy audit and dealer quotes work for EQIP and REAP.
The app will flag here and on Today when REAP reopens.

steps.t: Watch for reopening (the app checks weekly)
Line up an energy audit and quotes (same as EQIP)
Apply through your USDA Rural Development state office when it opens

changed.t: USDA cancelled the open REAP funding round and will take new applications after it rewrites the rules. Earlier applicants without a signed agreement must re-apply.

programs.warn: REAP is now “build first, apply later.” You pay for and install the project yourself, then apply 12–24 months after it’s finished. There’s no promise of a grant, so plan as if you’ll pay the full cost.
